turns.summary: Ride-hailing backend designed in Jakarta (Indonesia) to keep customer data local. Kubernetes is avoided by using Serverless App Engine (SAE) for the 8 microservices: user, ride, match, fare, pay, dispatch, rating, and notification. The architecture includes Cloud-native API Gateway with WAF protection, ALB, RDS for relational storage, Tair for caching, RocketMQ for messaging, and SLS for logs. Traffic flows from riders/drivers via ESA/DNS to the gateway. Open questions remain regarding specific instance sizes, high-availability configurations, and compliance details beyond data residency.

Selected Serverless App Engine (SAE) for eight microservices (user, driver, ride, dispatch, fare, payment, notification, rating) to meet the no-Kubernetes requirement. Logging is handled by SLS. The solution covers external access via rider/driver apps, with all components deployed across availability zones A and B for high availability.
